subject: Numeracy
title: Squares and triangles
objectives: Children will find squares and triangles around them.
Children will tell a circle from a square with support.
content: Finding and naming squares and triangles in the environment and telling circle, square and triangle apart.
teachingActivities: Trace each shape slowly with a finger; count corners and sides only for squares and triangles by touching; place shapes against real objects.
learnerActivities: Find squares and triangles, trace the shapes, sort circle, square and triangle, and make shape pictures.
resources: Boxes, tiles, triangle roof pictures, a slice of bread
assessment: Check whether each child names or points to a square, triangle and circle with support.
expectedOutcomes: Names or points to a square and a circle.
Points to a triangle when asked.
crossCurricular: Literacy: shape words and descriptive talk
Physical Development: tracing and carrying shapes
Understanding the world: buildings and objects

lessons.title: Square things
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will find and name squares in the environment.
successCriteria: Points to a square on request
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can find circles and round things, make patterns and use position words.
resources: A box, a floor tile and a window picture
lessons.starter: Hold up the cardboard square and say "This is a square. It has four straight sides and four corners." Trace its edge with a finger.
teacherActivities: Trace the square and count the four sides by touching each one. Count the corners.
Place the square against a box, a tile and a window picture. Say "Look, a square!"
Put a circle and a triangle beside the square and ask "Which is the square?"
Send children to find a square in the room.
learnerActivities: Children touch each side and corner and count to four.
Children point to the square shapes.
Child points to the square.
Children find square objects and show a friend.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Trace the square and count the four sides by touching each one. Count the corners. Children: Children touch each side and corner and count to four.
Step 2. Teacher: Place the square against a box, a tile and a window picture. Say "Look, a square!" Children: Children point to the square shapes.
Step 3. Teacher: Put a circle and a triangle beside the square and ask "Which is the square?" Children: Child points to the square.
Step 4. Teacher: Send children to find a square in the room. Children: Children find square objects and show a friend.

practical.title: Square hunt
steps: Give each pair a cardboard square.
Find things in the room that match its shape.
Bring one example back or point to it.
practical.safety: Use cardboard shapes with rounded corners; children walk and do not climb to reach objects.

differentiation.support: Offer a square and a circle only and hold them near the objects.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find three squares in different places.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many corners has a square?

expectedOutcomes: Names or points to a square
lessons.conclusion: Hold up the square and say "Square, square, square." Trace it in the air.
lessons.homeConnection: Look for squares at home such as tiles, windows or boxes.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find and name squares in the environment" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

pictures: A square, a box and a tile
learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Square, square, four straight sides. Square, square, four corners.

lessons.title: Triangle things
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will find and name triangles in the environment.
successCriteria: Points to a triangle on request
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can find circles and round things, make patterns and use position words.
resources: A roof picture, a sandwich cut in half, a drum stand picture
lessons.starter: Hold up the triangle. Say "This is a triangle. It has three straight sides and three corners." Trace its edge slowly.
teacherActivities: Trace the triangle and count three sides and three corners with the children.
Show a roof picture and a bread slice cut in half. Say "Triangle roof! Triangle bread!"
Place the triangle beside a circle and a square. Ask "Which is the triangle?"
Walk around the room and find triangle shapes.
learnerActivities: Children touch each side and corner and count to three.
Children point to the triangle shapes.
Child points to the triangle.
Children point to triangle shapes in the room.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Trace the triangle and count three sides and three corners with the children. Children: Children touch each side and corner and count to three.
Step 2. Teacher: Show a roof picture and a bread slice cut in half. Say "Triangle roof! Triangle bread!" Children: Children point to the triangle shapes.
Step 3. Teacher: Place the triangle beside a circle and a square. Ask "Which is the triangle?" Children: Child points to the triangle.
Step 4. Teacher: Walk around the room and find triangle shapes. Children: Children point to triangle shapes in the room.

practical.title: Triangle hunt
steps: Give each pair a cardboard triangle.
Match it to roof shapes, slices and pictures.
Tell a friend what you found.
practical.safety: Use cardboard shapes with rounded corners; no real knives; slices of bread cut by an adult before the lesson.

differentiation.support: Offer a triangle and a circle only.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a triangle and a square and say how they are different.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you show me a triangle?
How many sides has a triangle?

expectedOutcomes: Names or points to a triangle
lessons.conclusion: Trace a triangle in the air and say "Triangle, triangle, three sides."
lessons.homeConnection: Look for triangles on roofs, signs or sandwiches.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find and name triangles in the environment" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Triangle, triangle, three straight sides. Triangle, triangle, three sharp corners.

lessons.title: Circle, square or triangle?
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will sort circles, squares and triangles into three groups.
successCriteria: Puts shapes in the right group
Names or points to each shape
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can find circles and round things, make patterns and use position words.
resources: Large cardboard shapes in several colours
Three trays labelled with a circle, a square and a triangle
lessons.starter: Pull a shape from the bag and say "What shape is this? Let us find out." Feel it with your fingers first.
teacherActivities: Pull out a shape, trace its edge and say its name, then place it on the matching tray.
Let each child pull a shape from the bag, feel it and decide where it goes.
Mix up the shapes on the mat. Ask "Find all the circles."
Repeat for the squares and triangles.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say the shape name.
Child places the shape on the correct tray.
Children collect all circles.
Children sort each group into its tray.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pull out a shape, trace its edge and say its name, then place it on the matching tray. Children: Children watch and say the shape name.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child pull a shape from the bag, feel it and decide where it goes. Children: Child places the shape on the correct tray.
Step 3. Teacher: Mix up the shapes on the mat. Ask "Find all the circles." Children: Children collect all circles.
Step 4. Teacher: Repeat for the squares and triangles. Children: Children sort each group into its tray.

practical.title: Shape sorting trays
steps: Give each pair a bag of shapes and three trays.
Take turns to pull a shape and place it.
practical.safety: Use large cardboard or plastic shapes with smooth edges; keep them on the mat; supervise to avoid mouthing.

differentiation.support: Use two shapes only, a circle and a square, with a clear tray for each.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to sort shapes by shape and by colour and explain.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Which tray does it go in?
questions.expected: The tray with the same shape.

lessons.conclusion: Count the shapes in each tray together and say the shape name.
lessons.homeConnection: Sort plates, tiles and slices of bread by shape.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort circles, squares and triangles into three groups" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Shape pictures
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will make a simple picture using circles, squares and triangles.
successCriteria: Uses at least two different shapes in a picture
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can find circles and round things, make patterns and use position words.
lessons.starter: Show a picture of a house made of shapes. Say "This house has a square, a triangle roof and a round window. Let us make our own."
teacherActivities: Build a house on the paper with a square and a triangle roof. Say the shape names.
Give each child a few shapes and ask them to make a house or a car.
Walk around and ask "What shape is this?" for each child.
Display the pictures on a table and let children look at each other’s pictures.
learnerActivities: Children watch and point to the shapes.
Child places the shapes to make a picture.
Child names or points to a shape in their picture.
Children point to the shapes in a friend’s picture.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Build a house on the paper with a square and a triangle roof. Say the shape names. Children: Children watch and point to the shapes.
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child a few shapes and ask them to make a house or a car. Children: Child places the shapes to make a picture.
Step 3. Teacher: Walk around and ask "What shape is this?" for each child. Children: Child names or points to a shape in their picture.
Step 4. Teacher: Display the pictures on a table and let children look at each other’s pictures. Children: Children point to the shapes in a friend’s picture.

practical.title: Shape house pictures
steps: Give each child a sheet of paper and shapes.
Arrange the shapes to make a house.
Glue them down if they wish.
practical.safety: Use non-toxic glue sticks; supervise glue use; keep shapes large; wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Offer two shapes and show where to place them.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a picture of a boat or a car and name the shapes.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you find a square in your picture?

lessons.conclusion: Put the pictures on a display and say "Well done, shape builders."
lessons.homeConnection: Make a picture with cut-out shapes from old cartons.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make a simple picture using circles, squares and triangles" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Shape stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show they can find and name circles, squares and triangles at three stations.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can find circles and round things, make patterns and use position words.
lessons.starter: Sing the three shape songs and show the three stations.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
Ask "Show me a triangle" and "Which shape is this?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children play at each station.
Child points to or names a shape.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children play at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Show me a triangle" and "Which shape is this?" Children: Child points to or names a shape.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Use smooth large shapes only; supervise stations; keep glue supervised.

differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to quiz a friend: "Show me a square."

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names or points to a square and a circle; points to a triangle; sorts shapes.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 9
Recognises circle, square and triangle with support
lessons.conclusion: Sing the shape songs and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Look for shapes on the way home and name them.
